messages:
Maya: hi all, I joined today on infra. Trying to run `kubectl get pods -n staging` but I get `Error from server (Forbidden)`. Who handles kubeconfig/namespace RBAC?
Jun (eng-infra): welcome Maya! :wave: we manage onboarding. Can you share `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.current-context}'` and your company email?
Maya: context is `rwd-staging-eu`, email maya@redwood.com. my SSO shows group `engineering-developers`.
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-2399 for maya@redwood.com assigned to Jun. ETA 20m.
Jun (eng-infra): thanks. I see you don't have a RoleBinding in the `staging` ns. Two options:
1) add you to `devs` group in the namespace (recommended for humans)
2) create a short-lived serviceaccount and token for local work
If you want (2) run:```bash
kubectl -n staging create serviceaccount maya-local
kubectl -n staging create token maya-local --duration=8h
```Then set a context for it:```bash
TOKEN=\$(kubectl -n staging create token maya-local --duration=8h)
kubectl config set-credentials maya-local --token="$TOKEN"
kubectl config set-context maya-staging --cluster=rwd-staging-cluster --namespace=staging --user=maya-local
kubectl config use-context maya-staging
```
Maya: tried that, token created and `kubectl get pods` now works. Nice. Any tips to avoid accidentally running commands in prod?
Ravi: good call. We keep prod contexts named `rwd-prod-*` and add a kubectl plugin that warns on prod. Also we recommend `kubectl config rename-context` for clarity or set KUBECONFIG per terminal:```bash
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/maya-staging
```
Alex (sre): security note: serviceaccount tokens show up in audit logs; if you need elevated perms for demos, we do time-limited grants via Impersonation in the auth system and add an audit tag. Ping SRE for that.
Lina: FYI if your workstation is macOS and you're using kube-aws-sso, run `aws-sso login` first — we've seen timeouts cause Forbidden errors that look like RBAC problems.
Jun (eng-infra): done: created a RoleBinding for `group:engineering-developers` in `staging` so you won't need the token after today. You can delete the local creds with `kubectl config unset users.maya-local` if you want.
Maya: confirmed - both token and group binding work. Thank you all for the quick help and the warm welcome! :smile:
Jun (eng-infra): welcome aboard Maya. If you hit anything else DM me or drop into #eng-infra.
